bib.title: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235, 2024

question: Is using the same learning rate for the LoRA matrices A and B optimal when the model width is large, and if not, how should the rates be set?
hypothesis: With large width, equal learning rates for A and B prevent efficient feature learning; a larger rate for B than for A (fixed ratio) fixes this.
contributions: Infinite-width scaling analysis showing standard LoRA (same lr for A and B) is inefficient (Proposition 1, Theorem 1)
LoRA+: eta_B = lambda * eta_A with lambda>1 fixed, tuning only eta_A, same cost as LoRA
Experiments on RoBERTa-base, GPT-2 and Llama-7b showing 1-2% gains and up to ~2X speedup
Guidance on the ratio lambda (about 2^4 for RoBERTa Init[2]; 2^1-2^2 for Llama)

method.summary: Theory (toy linear model, then general architectures with Adam in the infinite-width limit) shows efficient LoRA needs eta_A = Theta(1/n) and eta_B = Theta(1). LoRA+ sets eta_B = lambda*eta_A and grid-searches eta_A; experiments sweep (eta_A, eta_B) grids on GLUE tasks with GPT-2/RoBERTa-base and on MNLI and flan-v2 with Llama-7b.
method.task: parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA) of language models; learning-rate scaling

other.width: paper says n≈700 for GPT2 (width remark)

other.lora_targets: q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, up_proj, down_proj, gate_proj

models.name: Toy MLP f(x)=Wout relu(BA relu(Win x))

training.objective: inferred: task loss (classification / instruction fine-tuning); toy model squared loss
training.optimizer: AdamW (GLUE: beta1=0.9, beta2=0.99, eps=1e-8; Llama: beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-6); toy model: gradient descent
training.lr: grid. GLUE: etaA in {4e-3,2e-3,1e-3,5e-4,2e-4,1e-4}, etaB in {8e-4,4e-4,2e-4,1e-4,5e-5,2e-5,1e-5} (as printed; figures show A on 1e-5..8e-4 and B on 1e-4..4e-3). Llama: etaA,etaB in {1e-6,5e-6,1e-5,2.5e-5,5e-5,1e-4}, etaB>=etaA (figures show wider ranges)
training.lr_schedule: GLUE: linear, no warmup; Llama: constant
training.seq_len: 128 (GLUE, Llama MNLI); Llama flan-v2 source 1536 / target 512
training.precision: FP16 (RoBERTa/GPT-2 main, Llama MNLI); full precision variants in App C.4; BF16 (Llama flan-v2)
training.hardware: Nvidia V100, Nvidia A10 (GLUE); V100 (Llama MNLI); A10 (Llama flan-v2)
training.seeds: GLUE 3 seeds; Llama 2 seeds for etaA=etaB and near-optimal, 1 otherwise; toy 3 seeds

other.lora_rank_alpha: RoBERTa/GPT-2 alpha=r=8 (also r=4 and r=16 in App C.6); Llama MNLI r=8 alpha=16; Llama flan-v2 r=64 alpha=16 (adapters on every linear layer excl. embeddings)
other.init: Init[1]: sigma_B^2=0, sigma_A^2=Theta(1/n); Init[2]: sigma_B^2=Theta(1), sigma_A^2=0; main text results use Init[2] unless stated
other.checkpointing: flan-v2: test accuracy of best checkpoint every 500 steps; Llama MNLI: best checkpoint

inference.samples: MMLU 5-shot; accuracy averaged over seeds as in training

metrics.name: test accuracy
metrics.definition: accuracy on task test set (GLUE, MNLI); MMLU average accuracy for flan-v2 models

metrics.name: test/train loss
metrics.definition: loss; shown as 100x loss in App C.5

baselines: standard LoRA with etaA = etaB (best equal-rate choice)
eval.protocol: grid sweep over (etaA, etaB); report best overall vs best with etaA≈etaB; averaged over seeds; fluctuations about 0.1% (GLUE); no significance test

evidence.where: Appendix C.1.2 (grid labels look swapped relative to the figure axes, where A runs 1e-5..8e-4 and B 1e-4..4e-3)

results.claim: LoRA+ improves performance by 1-2% and speeds finetuning up to ~2X at the same compute as LoRA.
results.setup: Abstract claim across experiments (RoBERTa, GPT-2, Llama-7b)

results.claim: Llama-7b trained 1 epoch on 100k flan-v2 subset gains roughly 1.3% MMLU with etaB >> etaA versus the best etaB = etaA.
results.setup: Llama-7b, flan-v2 100k, r=64, alpha=16, 2 seeds, Init[2], 5-shot MMLU; best checkpoint every 500 steps
results.quote: results in a roughly 1.3% gain compared with the optimal ηB = ηA
results.note: Reported as '%' in text; Fig 5 left shows best 44.0 MMLU acc, so likely points. Gain is vs best equal-rate setting.

results.claim: Llama-7b on MNLI: etaB = etaA is nearly optimal, so LoRA+ gives little gain on an easy task.
results.setup: Llama-7b, MNLI, 1 epoch, r=8, alpha=16, FP16, T=128
results.quote: In Figure 5, ηB = ηA is nearly optimal for all ηB ≥ηA.

results.claim: For RoBERTa with Init[2], a ratio lambda≈2^4 generally improves performance.
results.quote: setting a ratio of λ = ηB/ηA ≈24 improves performance

results.quote: the optimal ratio is smaller and is of order 22-23

results.claim: RoBERTa-base MNLI with etaB = 2^4 etaA reaches the same test accuracy about 2X faster than standard LoRA.
results.setup: RoBERTa-base on MNLI, etaA tuned by grid search in both setups (Fig 7)
results.note: Read from Fig 7 label; 'up to ~2X SpeedUp' in abstract.

results.claim: RoBERTa-base best test accuracy gap between optimal (etaA,etaB) and etaA≈etaB is larger for harder tasks (MNLI, QQP) than SST2, QNLI.
results.setup: RoBERTa-base, FP16, 3 epochs (10 SST2), T=128, 3 seeds
results.quote: the gap between the optimal choice of learning rates overall and the optimal choice when ηA ≈ηB is more pronounced for ‘harder’

results.claim: Efficient LoRA requires eta_B/eta_A = Theta(n); equal rates cannot be efficient.
results.setup: Infinite-width limit, Adam, single LoRA layer trainable, physics-level rigor; relies on Assumption 1
results.quote: LoRA Finetuning is efficient with ηA = Θ(n−1) and ηB = Θ(1).
results.note: Informal theorem; proof is non-rigorous per paper.

results.claim: Toy model: best train/test losses occur with etaB >> etaA; best at t=200 is (etaA,etaB)=(2.78,1.29e-4) per figure caption.
results.setup: Toy MLP n=100, r=4, d=5, 3 seeds, gradient descent, t=200
results.note: Caption's stated pair has etaA > etaB, which seems inconsistent with the text's 'etaB >> etaA'; possibly labels swapped in the caption. Equal-rate optimum is 2.15e-2 each.

results.claim: Llama flan-v2 with Init[1] has MMLU 0.6% higher than Init[2] and optimal ratio twice as large.
results.setup: Llama-7b flan-v2 100k, Init[1] vs Init[2] (App C.8, Fig 18b)
results.quote: the optimal MMLU accuracy is 0.6% higher than using Init[2] and the optimal ratio ηB/ηA is twice as large

limits: Optimal ratio lambda depends on model, task and initialization; analysis gives only the scaling (constants in Theta are intractable) and the authors leave refinement to future work.
Theory is of 'physics level of rigor', single-sample fine-tuning, a single trainable LoRA layer, and assumes mu-P pretraining; Theorem 1 relies on Assumption 1 and is stated informally.
Compute-limited GLUE runs (T=128, 3 epochs) give lower accuracies than Hu et al. 2021.
Train loss on flan-v2 did not favor etaB>etaA on grid tried; model overfits within one epoch (Fig 18 caption).
Only 7B Llama and small GLUE models; no larger widths or other PEFT variants tested.
Gains are larger on hard tasks and small on easy ones (MNLI for Llama).

terms.definition: set the learning rates for A, B such that ηB = ληA with λ > 1 fixed and tune ηA.
LoRA fine-tuning is stable and for all LoRA layers, all steps t>1, delta1_t and delta2_t = Theta(1).
